transcript.text: [photo notes-scene-screenshot.jpg: a Notes screenshot titled "Lighthouse - scene 4": Theo sets the ledger down, Mara says she kept the second chair, the lamp turns over the harbor] done!

Scene 4 is in the books, Jordan 🔥 "Somebody had to" is a great line, and so is Mara wiping a glass that's already dry. It came in around 90 words, so it's tighter than the 200 we aimed for. Paste the whole scene here so I can give you real feedback on it?

Theo set the ledger down on the counter and didn't open it. "You kept the second chair," he said. Mara shrugged, wiping a glass that was already dry. "Somebody had to." He sat. Neither of them said the name. Outside, the lamp turned over once, twice, and the harbor went white and dark again.

Here's my take. The unnamed name is the strongest part. "Neither of them said the name" lets the reader feel the weight without you explaining it. The lamp turning over at the end works too, because the light going white and dark again mirrors the tension. One thing to try: give Theo one small physical beat before he sits, so the pause before "He sat" carries even more.

You landed at about 90 words against the 200 target. What happened there: did the scene feel finished, or did the time run out?
